lawyer:
Abul Kalam Azad, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners.
Rabishanker Chakraborty, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Abdul Jabber and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Mohammed Sekander and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued at the instance of the pre-emptee against the judgment and order dated 22-7-92 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar in Misc. Appeal No. 55 of 1987, allowing pre-emption and reversing the judgment and order dated 7-6-87 passed by the Assistant Judge, Moheshkhali Cox's Bazar passed in the pre-emption Misc. Case No 17 of 1986 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Dismissing the prayer for pre-emption opposite party No. 1 filed pre-emption case against the present petitioner and others. Case of the pre-emptor, in short, is that the opposite party 2 to 4 sold the case land on 6-11-86 to the opposite party 1 without giving notice to the petitioner who is co-sharer of the seller by inheritance as his pre-decessor was an original settlement holder and the purchaser is a stranger. The pre-emptee has contested the case. Contending, inter alia, that since the original Zaminders settled the lands of which suit land is a part on 18-9-1908 along with other land to the pre-decessors-in-interest of the pre-emptor, named Semiruddin, Mukbul Ali and others, without mentioning the Khatian Number or plot Number of the same, the suit land cannot be pre-empted, as it cannot be treated as a part of a holding as defined in section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Trial Court dismissed the case for pre-emption finding, inter alia, that in absence of the Khatian Number and Plot Number the land which has been transferred cannot be termed as a part of a holding. Trial Court also found the pre-emptee is a co-sharer by purchase and thus dismissed the pre-emption case. 

 2. Pre-emptor's appeal which has been allowed by the impugned Judgment and order. Appellate court found that the case land is part of a holding which was originally settled in a compact manner giving its description with boundary and as such although the Khatian Number and Plot Number are not there, there is the original deed of settlement and the land which was settled is a holding and the case land is a part of it. The pre- emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance and also by prior purchase, as the pre-emptee is a subsequent purchaser the pre-emption was allowed by the appellate Court. Thus the trial Court wrongly and illegally found that the pr-emptee being a co-sharer, pre-emption cannot be allowed. 

 3. The appellate Court has rightly found that the pre-emptor is entitled to pre-empt the case land as a co-sharer, because he is a prior purchaser. Now the only question remains to be settled whether only because the Khatian Number and Plot Number are not there of the land in the deed under pre-emption it can be called part of the holding. Sub-section 1 of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act reads as follows: 

 In view of the aforesaid definition the land which was originally settled to the predecessors of the pre-emptor, forms a holding although there was no khatian or plot number, therefore, the land transferred under pre-emption can be called and termed as a part of holding. 

 5. Mr Azad cites an unreported decision pronounced in CR case No. 943 of 1989 on the same point by a Single Bench finding that the pre-emption cannot be allowed as there is no Khatian Number or Plot Number. The said decision is not binding upon this court. It has only persuasive force. After State Acquisition and Tenancy Act came in 1950 the owners and possessors of all kinds of lands have become direct tenants under the Government. The pre-emptor being a co-sharer and the purchaser, being stranger, case land being part of a holding that is portion of a compact land, although there is no Khatian Number or plot Number of the transferred land, it constitutes a part of an agriculture holding according to section 96(1) and section 2(13) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. So, pre-emption, in the instant case, is to be allowed. The pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has been filed within 4 (four) months from the date of knowledge. Appellate Court has rightly and legally allowed pre-emption. There is no illegality in the judgment and order of the appellate Court resulting in an error in. the decision occasioning failure of justice.
